description: List the 10 site/insurance-status groups with the largest share of conservation records. Return exactly 10, breaking ties at the cutoff arbitrarily.

c.request: Matching conservation records (`scanconservation`) to their sites on `zoneref` = `sites.zoneregistry` and dropping any without a site, which are the top 10 site reference and insurance status (`insurstat`) combinations by share of conservation records? Treat a missing status as its own value. Show the site reference, the insurance status, the record count, and the count as a fraction of all matched conservation records (unrounded), sorted by that fraction from highest to lowest with missing values last. List the 10 site/insurance-status groups with the largest share of conservation records. Return exactly 10, breaking ties at the cutoff arbitrarily.
c.sql: WITH matched AS (SELECT sc.zoneref, s.insurstat FROM scanconservation sc INNER JOIN sites s ON sc.zoneref = s.zoneregistry), totals AS (SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_matched FROM matched), grouped AS (SELECT zoneref, insurstat, COUNT(*) AS record_count FROM matched GROUP BY zoneref, insurstat) SELECT g.zoneref AS site_reference, g.insurstat AS insurance_status, g.record_count, g.record_count::double precision / t.total_matched AS share FROM grouped g CROSS JOIN totals t ORDER BY share DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 10;

a.request: Match each conservation record (`scanconservation`) to its site where `sites.zoneregistry` equals `scanconservation.zoneref`, and drop records with no matching site. For each combination of site reference (`zoneref`) and insurance status (`insurstat`), with a missing status kept as its own value, show the site reference, the insurance status, the number of conservation records, and that number as a fraction of all matched conservation records, unrounded. Sort by that fraction from highest to lowest (missing last) and return exactly 10 rows, breaking any ties at 10th place arbitrarily.
a.sql: SELECT c.zoneref AS site_reference, s.insurstat AS insurance_status, COUNT(*) AS record_count, COUNT(*)::numeric / SUM(COUNT(*)) OVER () AS fraction FROM scanconservation c JOIN sites s ON s.zoneregistry = c.zoneref GROUP BY c.zoneref, s.insurstat ORDER BY fraction DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 10;

b.request: Top 10 (zoneref→sites.zoneregistry inner-joined) site_reference × insurstat groups, ranked by count / total matched scanconservation rows (NULL insurstat kept as its own group, unrounded fraction, NULLS LAST, ties at position 10 broken arbitrarily)
b.sql: WITH matched AS (SELECT sc.zoneref, s.insurstat FROM scanconservation sc INNER JOIN sites s ON sc.zoneref = s.zoneregistry), total AS (SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM matched), grouped AS (SELECT zoneref AS site_reference, insurstat, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM matched GROUP BY zoneref, insurstat) SELECT g.site_reference, g.insurstat, g.cnt, g.cnt * 1.0 / t.n AS fraction FROM grouped g CROSS JOIN total t ORDER BY fraction DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 10;

d.request: Among the site reference and insurance status combinations from matched conservation records (`scanconservation` joined to `sites` on `zoneref` = `sites.zoneregistry`, with unmatched records dropped and a missing insurance status treated as its own value), which 10 groups have the largest share of conservation records? Return exactly 10, breaking ties at the cutoff arbitrarily, and show the site reference, insurance status, record count, and unrounded fraction of all matched conservation records for each, sorted from highest to lowest fraction with missing values last.
d.sql: SELECT s.zoneregistry AS site_reference, s.insurstat AS insurance_status, COUNT(*) AS record_count, COUNT(*) * 1.0 / SUM(COUNT(*)) OVER () AS fraction FROM scanconservation c JOIN sites s ON c.zoneref = s.zoneregistry GROUP BY s.zoneregistry, s.insurstat ORDER BY fraction DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 10;
